Routing notes:
- Confirmed successful choice: C (regional office) for:
  - Large shipment, south region
  - Small shipment, north region
  - Small invoice, south region
- C was rejected for:
  - Large claim, north region
  - Small claim, south region
  - Small refund, south region
- B (priority desk) was rejected for:
  - Small invoice, east region
  - Small invoice, north region
  - Large claim, north region
- No successful examples for A or D.
- Do not assume urgency/requester wording determines routing; “before end of day,” repeated attempts, and client follow-ups did not establish a reliable rule.
- Strongest current signal: shipments route to C in both observed north/south cases. C may also apply to some south-region invoices, but not claims/refunds. Avoid choosing C automatically for non-shipment requests.

Routing notes:
- C (regional office) is confirmed for:
  - Small shipments, north and south regions
  - Large shipment, south region
  - Small invoice, south region
- Requester wording does not appear to determine routing. Repeated follow-ups, second attempts, urgency, and “regional office” wording did not change outcomes.
- C was rejected for:
  - Large claim, north region
  - Small claim, south region
  - Small refund, south region
- A (standard queue) has now been rejected for:
  - Small refund, east region
  - Large refund, east region
  - Small invoice, east region
  - Small claims, east and south regions
  - Small refunds, south and north regions
  Avoid A for these request types; it may be broadly invalid, not merely a fallback.
- B (priority desk) was rejected for:
  - Small invoice, east and north regions
  - Large claim, north region
- No successful examples for B, A, or D. No successful example for D at all.
- Strongest rule remains: shipments route to C across observed north/south cases, including urgent and repeated requests.
- C may apply to some south-region invoices, but do not generalize it to claims or refunds. Claims/refunds remain unresolved across regions; avoid A and use further evidence before selecting another option.

Routing notes:
- Requester wording, urgency, sender/team, and follow-up status do not reliably determine routing. “Regional office” wording coincided with one C success but is not sufficient evidence.
- C is confirmed for:
  - Small invoice, south region
  - Small shipments, north and south regions (but one later small north shipment was rejected, so verify rather than assume)
  - Large shipment, south region (one success and one rejection; not universal)
- C was rejected for:
  - Large claim, north region
  - Small claim, south region
  - Small refund, south region
  - Large shipment, south region
  - Small shipment, north region
  Treat shipment rules as inconsistent across cases.
- A is rejected for:
  - Small invoice, east and north regions
  - Small claims, east and south regions
  - Small refunds, east, south, and north regions
  - Large refund, east region
  Avoid A for these types; it may be broadly invalid.
- B is confirmed for large refund, south region (one success), but rejected for small invoice, east and north regions and large claim, north region.
- D has no successful examples and was rejected for large refund, south; large invoice, north; large claim, east and south. Avoid D unless new evidence supports it.
- Claims remain unresolved across regions; avoid A, C, and D where rejected, and gather evidence before choosing B.
- Refund routing is uncertain: A and C have rejections, D rejected, while B succeeded for a large south refund.

Routing notes:
- Requester wording, urgency, sender/team, and follow-up status are unreliable routing signals. “Regional office” coincided with successes but is not sufficient evidence.
- C successes: small invoice/south; small shipments/north and south; large shipment/south (one success). C was later rejected for large shipment/south, so shipment routing is inconsistent.
- C rejections: large claim/north, small claim/south, small refund/south, small shipment/north, and large shipment/south. Verify every shipment and avoid C where specifically rejected.
- B successes: large refund/south; small refund/south; large claim/south (two successes); small claim/east.
- B rejections: small invoice/east and north; large claim/north; large refund/east; large invoice/north; large shipment/east. Do not generalize B by type or region.
- A rejections: small invoice/east and north; small claims/east and south; small refunds/east, south, and north; large refund/east; large claim/north. Avoid A for these; it may be broadly invalid.
- D has no successful examples. Rejected for large refund/south, large invoice/north, and large claims/east and south. Avoid D unless new evidence supports it.
- Claims are region-dependent: B works for large claim/south and small claim/east, but is rejected for large claim/north; A and C also have claim rejections. Gather evidence before routing.
- Refunds remain uncertain: B works for large and small refunds in the south but fails for large refund/east; A, C, and D have rejections.
- Treat all type/size/region combinations as case-specific; prefer confirmed combinations and verify conflicting patterns.

Routing notes:
- Wording, urgency, sender/team, and follow-up status are unreliable routing signals. “Regional office” and similar phrasing do not determine the option.
- Treat every type/size/region combination as case-specific; prefer confirmed outcomes and verify conflicts.
- C successes: small invoice/south; small shipments/north and south; large shipment/south (one success). New rejection: small shipment/south. C also rejected large claim/north, small claim/south, small refund/south, small shipment/north, and large shipment/south.
- B successes: large refund/south; small refund/south (but now contradicted by a rejection); large claim/south (multiple successes); small claim/east and south; large claim/east.
- B rejections: small shipment/north; small refund/east and south; small invoice/east and north; large claim/north; large refund/east; large invoice/north; large shipment/east and south. Do not generalize B by type or region.
- A successes: large shipment/east. Rejections: small invoice/east and north; small claims/east and south; small refunds/east, south, and north; large refund/east; large claim/north; large invoice/north. A may be broadly invalid except confirmed cases.
- D has no successes. Rejected for large refund/south, large invoice/north, and large claims/east and south. Avoid D absent new evidence.
- Claims are highly region-dependent: B works for large claim/south and east, and small claim/east and south, but fails for large claim/north. Gather evidence before routing.
- Refunds are inconsistent: B has successes for south refunds but a newer small-refund/south rejection; it fails for large refund/east and small refund/east. A, C, and D also have rejections.

Routing notes:
- Wording, urgency, sender/team, and follow-up status are unreliable routing signals. “Regional office” does not determine the option.
- Treat every type/size/region combination as case-specific; rely on confirmed outcomes and verify conflicts.
- C successes: small invoice/south (multiple); small shipments/north and south; large shipment/south; large invoice/north; large refund/east. C rejections: small invoice/east; small claim/south; small refund/south; small shipment/north; large claim/north; large shipment/south. Do not generalize C by region or type.
- B successes: large refund/south; large claim/south (multiple); large claim/east; small claim/east and south. B rejections: large refund/north; small refund/east and south (including recent confirmation); small invoice/east and north; small shipment/north; large claim/north; large refund/east; large invoice/north; large shipment/east and south.
- A successes: large shipment/east (multiple). Rejections: small invoice/east and north; small claims/east and south; small refunds/east, south, and north; large refund/east; large claim/north; large invoice/north. A remains unsuitable except for confirmed large shipment/east.
- D has no successes. Rejected for large refund/south, large invoice/north, and large claims/east and south. Avoid D absent new evidence.
- Claims are region-dependent: B works for large claim/south and east and small claim/east and south; C failed for small claim/south; B fails for large claim/north.
- Refunds remain inconsistent: C works for large refund/east; B works for large refund/south but fails for large refund/north/east and small refund/south/east. Gather evidence before routing.
